basis: The Fed raised rates 25 bp to 3.75%-4.00%; the unanimous vote and projections showing another likely 2026 hike were incrementally hawkish.
At the cash close, Dow fell 1.21%, S&P 500 fell 0.44%, and Nasdaq was nearly flat; the dollar strengthened and the Treasury curve flattened as the initial relief response reversed.

The 6:00 PM ET futures reopen is a new liquidity regime. Penalize gaps and extensions, require completed 5m/15m acceptance after reopen, and distinguish continuation from mean-reversion of the Fed shock.

Gold and silver remain vulnerable to the stronger dollar and higher short yields, but oversold momentum and bullish divergence can produce fast rebounds. Do not chase either direction without a structural stop.
Crude remains driven primarily by supply rerouting, inventories, and war headlines; the Fed is secondary. Thin overnight liquidity increases false-break and wick risk.
